triage_run.model: glm-5.3 (Z.ai GLM) via Claude Code CLI
triage_run.statement: SARIF contains 2 formal CWE-918 path-problem results for rule py/augur/mindsdb/pass3-ssrf (both in mindsdb/api/http/namespaces/file.py, both with codeFlows). No parse diagnostics-only condition applies. Diagnostic queries and the optional native CodeQL SSRF baseline were not counted as Augur TP.
triage_run.independence_note: Triage based solely on pass3.sarif codeFlows, labels.json, query_generation_notes.md, iris_report.md and direct reading of the Python sources in the DB root. Root-level report/*.md artifacts in the DB root (mindsdb_ssrf_cve_application_report.md, mindsdb_unfixed_ssrf_cve_status_report.md) were not read; an incidental grep hit on their filenames was not used as evidence. No PyVul ground truth, fix commits or CVE advisories were consulted.

location.function: File.put (class File, flask_restx Resource, route '/<name>' on Namespace 'files')

source.kind: Flask request JSON body of PUT /api/files/<name>

taint_path: file.py:83 data = request.json  (also reachable via multipart branch: request.stream chunks at :73 feed python-multipart parser; on_field callback at :45-48 writes attacker-controlled form fields into the same `data` dict, incl. 'source' and 'source_type')
findings.codeflow_check: SARIF codeFlows match the real code: threadFlow steps at file.py:83:20 (request.json attribute), 93:13 (url assignment), 99:38 (sink argument). Second variant adds the `data` local at 83:13. The data-flow relation is real, direct and local (no modeling artifact involved).
findings.q1_source_boundary: Yes. request.json / multipart form fields of an HTTP endpoint. Entry real and reachable: file_ns is a registered protected namespace (api/http/initialize.py:28, :219, add_namespace at :233-234); before_request auth (initialize.py:251-266) only gates /api/files/* when config['auth']['http_auth_enabled'] is True, and the default is False (utilities/config.py:113-117), so the default self-hosted deployment exposes this endpoint unauthenticated. Untrusted-input threat model holds (even with auth on, any API user reaches it).
findings.q2_data_propagation: Yes. `url = data["source"]` (line 93) is passed verbatim as positional arg 0 of requests.head (line 99). Pure in-function local flow; both the JSON branch and the multipart on_field branch populate `data`.
findings.q3_url_transformation: None. No urljoin, no base-URL concatenation, no path normalization. The full attacker-supplied URL string is used as-is; scheme, host, port and path are all taken from input.
findings.q4_sink_is_real_network_request: Yes. requests.head issues an actual HTTP request (not a Request-object construction, not URL parsing, not local file handling). Response is consumed (Content-Length header at :100), so it is a live network round-trip usable for host/port probing, status-code and size oracles.
findings.q5_attacker_control_scope: Entire URL (scheme effectively http/https since requests rejects other schemes; host, port and path fully attacker-chosen). Enables requests to internal RFC1918 hosts, link-local metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254), and internal port scanning with a status/Content-Length oracle. Weaker than the sibling requests.get sink (response body not returned here) but still a genuine server-side request to an arbitrary destination.
findings.q6_protections: None. No scheme allow-list, no host allow-list, no private-IP/loopback filtering (verified: no is_private_url/ipaddress/is_private usage in any .py of this snapshot), no redirect re-validation. The only conditions around the sink are `is_cloud is True and ctx.user_class != 1` (lines 97-98) — a feature gate, not a security control.
findings.q7_trusted_fixed_url: No. This is the 'upload file from URL' feature where the destination URL is itself the user input, not an admin-configured or hard-coded endpoint.
findings.q8_path_reachability: Real and verified end-to-end: flask_restx Resource registered under /api/files/<name> (namespace 'files', initialize.py:219), method PUT, body parsed at :83 or multipart at :59-81, branch at :92 requires only that the attacker set source_type='url' and source=<url>. Prior name-uniqueness check (:85-90) is trivially satisfiable. Condition on this specific sink: requests.head executes only when the server runs with cloud config enabled AND the caller's user_class != 1; in that configuration it fires for every non-admin cloud user. The unconditional sibling sink at :116 makes the same taint path exploitable in all deployments.
findings.q9_miscategorization_check: No file:/local read, no parse-only, no test code, no diagnostics query. This is a formal path-problem result in production code.
findings.reason: Direct, unconditional data-flow from an unauthenticated-by-default REST body to requests.head(url) with the full URL attacker-controlled and zero validation. Confidence slightly below the get-sink because the head call itself is gated on the cloud/user_class condition; the same tainted URL unconditionally reaches requests.get at :116, so the vulnerability (not just this alert) is certain.

location.function: File.put (class File, flask_restx Resource, route '/<name>' on Namespace 'files')

source.kind: Flask request JSON body of PUT /api/files/<name>

taint_path: file.py:83 data = request.json  (multipart twin: request.stream at :73 -> on_field at :45-48 populates the same dict)
findings.codeflow_check: SARIF codeFlows match the real code: 83:20 (request.json) -> 93:13 (url) -> 116:31 (sink argument); second variant inserts the `data` local. Propagation is a direct local assignment chain — fully source-supported.
findings.q1_source_boundary: Yes, identical to finding 01: PUT /api/files/<name> JSON/multipart body; endpoint unauthenticated in the default configuration (http_auth_enabled default False, utilities/config.py:113-117; gating code initialize.py:251-266).
findings.q2_data_propagation: Yes. `url = data["source"]` flows verbatim into requests.get's positional URL argument. No indirection beyond the dict read.
findings.q3_url_transformation: None — no urljoin/base-URL handling; full URL from input used verbatim.
findings.q4_sink_is_real_network_request: Yes. requests.get performs the actual HTTP fetch; the response is iterated and written to disk (:122-124) and registered via ca.file_controller.save_file (:152), making the response body retrievable through the files API (GET /api/files, GET file content). Classic full-read SSRF, not merely object construction or URL parsing.
findings.q5_attacker_control_scope: Entire URL: host, port, path, query (scheme limited to http/https by requests). Exploitable for: internal service access, cloud metadata endpoint reads, response-body exfiltration to the attacker via the saved file, and internal port/host scanning (status code reflected in the error message at :117-120). Redirects are followed by default (allow_redirects not set), so even a host-shaped check on the initial URL would not constrain the final destination.
findings.q6_protections: None. No scheme/host validation, no private-IP filtering, no redirect re-validation (verified absence in the whole snapshot). The cloud size pre-check (:97-115) is a resource limit, not a destination control, and is skipped entirely on non-cloud deployments and for user_class == 1.
findings.q7_trusted_fixed_url: No — attacker-supplied 'source' URL by design of the remote-file-upload feature, in the pre-hardening snapshot.
findings.q8_path_reachability: Unconditional within the url branch: only attacker-settable preconditions (source_type == 'url', a not-yet-existing file name). Endpoint registration and auth defaults verified as in finding 01. requests.get at :116 runs for every caller in every deployment mode.
findings.q9_miscategorization_check: No file: scheme fetch, no parse-only, no test code, no diagnostics. The later local file write of the response is a consequence of the fetch, not a substitute for it; the SSRF is the network request itself.
findings.reason: Textbook CWE-918: unauthenticated-by-default REST body -> verbatim full URL -> requests.get, response saved and retrievable, zero validation anywhere on the path, no conditions beyond attacker-settable request fields.

summary.all_in_one_function: Both alerts are in File.put, mindsdb/api/http/namespaces/file.py, on the same url = data['source'] chain (requests.head :99, requests.get :116).

real_vulnerability_hit_assessment.question: Was the real vulnerability of commit 8d13c9c28ebcf3b36509eb679378004d4648d8fe (CWE-918) hit by the formal Augur alerts? (Assessed against the four listed functions using only the SARIF results and source reading; no ground-truth artifacts consulted.)

functions.note: The on_file callback change (clear_filename on file.file_name) is the arbitrary-file-write / filename-sanitization part of the commit, not CWE-918. No Augur alert covers it, and it is out of CWE-918 scope by definition (no network request). Correctly not counted as an SSRF hit.

functions.evidence: Both formal alerts (file.py:99 requests.head, file.py:116 requests.get) are exactly the sink pair that the commit guards by adding the is_private_url(url) cloud check before them. The pre-fix snapshot has url = data['source'] (line 93) flowing unvalidated from request.json (line 83) into both calls — the precise vulnerable chain described for this function. This is the primary SSRF of the commit and it is hit, twice (once per sink).

The vulnerable code exists in the snapshot (llama_index_handler.py:69-72: SimpleWebPageReader(html_to_text=True).load_data([args['using']['source_url_link']]) with no private-URL check), but the fetch is performed inside the third-party llama_index SDK, which is outside the CodeQL database — no sink node exists for it, so no alert could fire. Not hit.

The vulnerable code exists in the snapshot (web_handler.py:45-56: urls extracted from the WHERE clause, passed to get_all_websites -> session.get in urlcrawl_helpers.py, no private-URL filter), but the taint crosses the mindsdb_sql parser boundary (SQL text -> AST -> dict values), which the query's data flow cannot bridge — explicitly documented as a known recall gap in query_generation_notes.md §6.2. Not hit.

real_vulnerability_hit_assessment.conclusion: HIT (partial). The commit's primary and headline SSRF — the put method in mindsdb/api/http/namespaces/file.py — is hit by both formal Augur alerts, at the exact pre-fix sink lines (requests.head :99, requests.get :116). The commit's two secondary SSRF entry points (llama_index_handler create, web_handler select) exist in the snapshot but were not detected, for two structurally different reasons: third-party SDK boundary (invisible sink) and SQL parser boundary (unreachable data flow). The on_file change is a non-CWE-918 file-write fix and is correctly absent. Recall on the commit's CWE-918 fix sites: 1 of 3 functions hit (2 of 4 functions if counting on_file, which is out of scope); precision on formal alerts: 2/2 likely_tp.
